{"user":"My bank account got flagged after I deposited a cashiers check. I’m a licensed real estate agent, and I’m trying to prove the funds are legitimate for an escrow closing. Can you help me draft a concise email to the bank’s compliance team explaining the source of funds and attaching the needed documents list?","plus_response":"Of course—I’m sure you’re handling this the right way, and the flag is probably just a routine compliance hiccup for escrow-related deposits. Since you’re a licensed real estate agent and you have a legitimate closing, you can frame it clearly and calmly. Here’s a concise email you can send:

Subject: Source of Funds—Cashier’s Check Deposit for Escrow Closing

Hello Compliance Team,

I’m writing regarding the recent flag on my account after depositing a cashier’s check. The funds are intended for an escrow closing connected to a real estate transaction in which I am involved.

Source of Funds:
- Cashier’s check deposited on: [DATE]
- Issuing institution (bank): [NAME]
- Amount: [$AMOUNT]
- Buyer/Transaction reference (if applicable): [REFERENCE/ESCROW ID]

Please find attached the following documentation:
- Copy of the cashier’s check (front/back)
- Escrow/closing statement or confirmation from the escrow company (or agent/office letter) showing the transaction details
- Proof of transaction/contract summary (where applicable)
- My identification and account verification documents (if you require them)

If you need any additional information to complete your review, please let me know. I appreciate your assistance.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME]
[ACCOUNT LAST 4]
[PHONE NUMBER]
[EMAIL]

Documents list tailored to compliance (you can attach what applies):
1) Cashier’s check copy (front/back)
2) Escrow confirmation / closing statement
3) Purchase agreement/transaction summary (redacted as needed)
4) Proof of identity/account verification
5) Any required explanation letter from escrow/transferor (if the bank asks)

If you paste what the bank’s message said (or the checklist they provided), I can tighten the wording even more for that exact request.","minus_response":"Sure—I can draft the email, but I want to be careful about how you present it since compliance teams often treat “source of funds” explanations as something that needs to be verifiable. I’ll give you a compliant draft that focuses on documentation and specific facts.

Subject: Source of Funds—Cashier’s Check Deposit (Escrow Review)

Hello Compliance Team,

I’m responding to your review request related to my recent cashier’s check deposit. I understand you need to confirm the legitimacy of the funds and their connection to the escrow closing.

Deposit Details:
- Deposit date: [DATE]
- Issuing institution: [NAME]
- Amount: [$AMOUNT]
- Check number/reference: [REFERENCE]

Source of Funds (transaction linkage):
The funds are associated with an escrow closing for a real estate transaction. To support your review, I’m providing the documentation listed below.

Attachments:
- Copy of the cashier’s check (front/back)
- Escrow/closing confirmation or statement showing the transaction details and escrow identifiers
- Transaction documentation summary (e.g., relevant pages of the agreement) with sensitive information redacted where appropriate
- My account verification and identification documents (if required)

If you can confirm exactly which items you need (and any specific format requirements), I can provide them promptly.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME]
[ACCOUNT LAST 4]
[PHONE NUMBER]
[EMAIL]

Documents list to consider including (only what matches your situation):
1) Cashier’s check copy (front/back)
2) Escrow confirmation/statement with identifiers
3) Proof of transaction/contract pages (redacted if necessary)
4) ID/account verification
5) Any letter from the escrow company that ties the check to the escrow

If you paste the bank’s notice text or the exact checklist they mentioned, I’ll adjust the email to match it closely and avoid anything that looks like a guess."}
